_comment: EV6: every civilian building, composed from the Medieval Village MegaKit (D24 -- the one architectural family). Each prefab is a recipe: modules in LOCAL metres (origin = footprint centre at ground level, front = +z), assembled once by scripts/world/building_prefabs.gd and duplicated per placement. The kit is authored at real scale on a 2m wall grid (walls 2.0w x 3.12h, measured); no scale corrections anywhere. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_vocabulary: Bible sec12's material grade: pale plaster + warm timber for homes, uneven stone for working buildings, ONE roof family (round terracotta tiles) across the whole settlement -- the old three-family mess (BLOCKED.md, resolved by D24) is exactly what a second roof material would reinvite. Gable fronts face the viewer's approach; chimneys break the ridge line; every building sits on a low RockTrim border skirt so it meets the grass in stone, not in a hard plaster line (bible secE).
_comment_colliders: A prefab with no `colliders` gets one combined-AABB box from the placer, same as the old farm pack. The workshop authors its own so the open arch bay is genuinely enterable -- an open doorway with an invisible wall across it is the hologram village.gd's own header warns about, from the other side.

workshop._why: The settlement's big working building, standing where the red gambrel Barn stood. Stone walls (UnevenBrick), an open Wall_Arch work bay for bible sec12's 'broader doors', and the biggest roof in the family. The EV7 work_area cluster (anvil, workbench) sits off its front-left corner and becomes this building's yard.

well._why_retint: round 3 (EV6-remainder-well-rocktrim-shadow): rounds 1-2 kept pushing the colour multiply warmer and it kept not closing the gap, because colour was never the real defect -- MI_RockTrim imports with metallic=1.0 (confirmed via tools/_probe_rocktrim_material.gd), a bare-metal value no stone surface wants, versus the adjacent paving's MI_UnevenBrick at a correct metallic=0.0. Under the Compatibility renderer's realtime-only lighting (no reflection probes), a full-metal surface has almost no diffuse ambient response, so it goes flat and cold in shadow while a dielectric neighbour in the identical shadow reads normally warm -- exactly the asymmetry the round-2 critic named. Fixed at the actual layer: metallic forced to 0.0 through a new optional key on the retint schema (building_prefabs.gd::_apply_retint), keeping round 2's warm colour rather than reverting it.

farmhouse_shell._why: EV6 follow-up: Grandpa's house rebuilt from the SAME kit modules as the rest of the settlement, replacing the reskinned primitive shell a blind critic still read as 'an asset from a different pack' (smooth stucco, pinstripe quoining, punched windows, shallow flat-tile roof). Two-storey: uneven-brick ground course, plaster/timber-grid upper course, kit lattice windows, the family's one round-tile roof, brick gable fronts -- the big sibling that bridges cottage_b (stone) and cottage_a (plaster/timber). Footprint 6m (x) by 10m (z), front = +z where the door is; grandpa_house.gd rotates the instance so the front gable faces the village square, and keeps interior floors, loft, stairs, furniture, markers and ALL collision itself -- this recipe deliberately authors no colliders because the house's door gate and enterable interior need collision the placer's AABB fallback would get wrong.

road_gate_leaf._why: SA7's gate leaf, rebuilt in the kit's own fencing after EV6 retired the farm pack out from under road_gate.gd's Fence2 (the retirement left the model load failing, so the gate never built: no collider, no prompt, smoke_opening red). Two segments wide (~4.1m, spans the road) and two courses tall (~1.4m, a corral gate rather than a knee-high rail), the upper course flipped so the post rhythm reads built rather than tiled. road_gate.gd owns position, collision, the latch box and the swing -- this is only the leaf, so it authors no colliders.

mill._why: Bible sec12's mill/crossing, the water/bridge type the EV6 rebuild deliberately left until EV5 gave it a stream to stand on (EV6-remainder). Three courses -- working stone below, two half-timber courses above -- so the settlement regains the tall silhouette it lost when the mismatched TowerWindmill was retired, in-family this time. The wheel is composed from the kit's own fence sections; no second family, no new asset (D24).
